generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Sample from a pool of 60+ distinct uppercase surnames/given names; 20-50% of rows reuse a value already used (duplicates for DISTINCT); include near-variants (case-flipped, one-letter edits) of listed equality literals; never NULL for PK columns.
generic_sampling_rules.text_nullable: Same as text_name but 5-30% of rows are NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_grade: Sample integers in [-1, 6] with boundary emphasis at -1, 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6; 5-30% NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_classroom: Sample integers in [101, 112] with boundary emphasis at 106, 107, 108, 109, 110, 111; allow NULL foreign keys on child side.
generic_sampling_rules.fresh_values_share: About 50-70% of text values are fresh (not seen in the original sample); the rest are drawn from the observed pool to create duplicates and ties.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_mutation: For boundary-pool draws, restrict mutations to case-flip and single-character edit only; do not append or prepend arbitrary characters.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For each nullable column, plant NULLs at the compact database's observed share for that column, with a floor of 5% and at least one NULL row per nullable column per instance; PK/NOT NULL columns never get NULL.

dependencies.note: Soft join: list.Classroom may reference teachers.Classroom; NULL allowed on child side; parent rows may have no children. Child draws use only non-NULL parent values; teachers.Classroom may itself contain NULLs (parent side) and those NULL parents are excluded from child draws. Mix parent values with NULLs and sampled boundary/range values so each instance has both NULL and non-NULL rows; non-NULL values include boundary targets 106-111. Apply NULL rule after fill so at least one NULL and one non-NULL remain.

supporting_evidence.list.Classroom: Original values 101-112; statistics distinct=12; boundary targets 106-111.

supporting_evidence.names: Original name pools show uppercase surnames/given names; near-variants from equality literals in atomic operations.
supporting_evidence.pk_not_null: Schema declares PRIMARY KEY(LastName, FirstName) on both tables; SQLite PK columns are NOT NULL, so list.FirstName/list.LastName and teachers.FirstName/teachers.LastName never get NULL.

uncertainty: The join between list.Classroom and teachers.Classroom is not declared as a foreign key in the schema; treated as a soft join with NULLs allowed. list.FirstName and list.LastName are PK components and therefore NOT NULL; the null_rows atomic pattern for them is satisfied by the schema constraint rather than by planted NULLs. list.Classroom must contain both NULL and non-NULL rows with boundary targets reachable; the FK fill must not overwrite the entire sampled column. teachers.Classroom may contain NULLs on the parent side; soft-join child draws exclude NULL parent values. NULL shares for list.Classroom and teachers.Classroom follow the compact database share with a 5% floor; only list.Grade has an explicit 5-30% share.
